demos.title: 5-inch drone frame
demos.summary: A quadcopter X-frame, built up from a plate to a flight-ready frame.
steps: A 5-inch quadcopter X-frame bottom plate, 4 mm thick: a 40 x 40 mm center body and four 16 mm wide arms, 220 mm motor-to-motor across the diagonal. Only this base shape for now: no holes, slots, cutouts or fillets yet.
Add a 16 x 16 mm M3 hole pattern with a 6 mm center hole at the tip of each arm for the motors. Keep everything else exactly as it is.
Add a 30.5 x 30.5 mm M3 hole pattern in the center body for the flight controller. Keep everything else exactly as it is.
Cut a 60 mm long, 6 mm wide weight-saving slot along the middle of each arm. Keep everything else exactly as it is.
Round the outer corners of the center body and the arm tips with 3 mm fillets. Keep everything else exactly as it is.

demos.title: Desk phone stand
demos.summary: A printable stand that holds a phone at a comfortable viewing angle.
steps: A desk phone stand: an 80 mm wide, 90 mm deep base, a back support leaning back at 65 degrees, and a front lip that holds phones up to 12 mm thick. Only this base shape for now: no holes, slots, cutouts or fillets yet.
Cut a 12 mm wide slot through the front lip and the base for a charging cable. Keep everything else exactly as it is.
Round all outside edges with 2 mm fillets. Keep everything else exactly as it is.

demos.title: Desk cable clip
demos.summary: A screw-on clip that keeps three charging cables on the desk.
steps: A desk cable clip: a 60 x 20 x 4 mm base plate with three round cable cradles for 6 mm cables standing on top. Only this base shape for now: no holes, slots, cutouts or fillets yet.
Add two countersunk holes for M3 screws in the base, one at each end. Keep everything else exactly as it is.
Round the four vertical corners of the base plate with 2 mm fillets. Keep everything else exactly as it is.

demos.title: Under-desk headphone hook
demos.summary: A hook that screws under the desk and holds a pair of headphones.
steps: An under-desk headphone hook, 25 mm wide: a 50 x 40 x 5 mm mounting plate, a 60 mm drop, and a 45 mm deep hook arm. Only this base shape for now: no holes, slots, cutouts or fillets yet.
Add a 10 mm tall lip at the end of the hook arm so the headphones cannot slide off. Keep everything else exactly as it is.
Add two countersunk M4 screw holes in the mounting plate. Keep everything else exactly as it is.

demos.title: Raspberry Pi base tray
demos.summary: A tray with standoffs and vents for a Raspberry Pi 4.
steps: A base tray for a Raspberry Pi 4: 95 x 66 mm, a 2 mm floor and 10 mm tall, 2 mm thick walls. Only this base shape for now: no holes, slots, cutouts or fillets yet.
Add four 6 mm tall M2.5 standoffs on a 58 x 49 mm pattern on the floor. Keep everything else exactly as it is.
Cut a row of 3 mm wide ventilation slots in the floor between the standoffs. Keep everything else exactly as it is.
Cut openings in one short wall for the USB and Ethernet ports. Keep everything else exactly as it is.

demos.title: L-bracket
demos.summary: A stiff 90-degree bracket with countersunk mounting holes.
steps: An L-bracket: two 40 x 30 mm legs at 90 degrees, 4 mm thick. Only this base shape for now: no holes, slots, cutouts or fillets yet.
Add two countersunk M4 holes in each leg. Keep everything else exactly as it is.
Add a triangular 4 mm thick gusset between the legs in the middle of the bracket. Keep everything else exactly as it is.
